automation.title: Automation Rules
automation.description: Rules that run automatically on deals. Each rule watches one stage of one pipeline and, once a deal has stayed in it for the set number of hours, unassigns the deal so it returns to the pool.

when.pipeline: When a deal is in pipeline

automation.summary: When a deal stays in {pipeline} › {stage} for {duration}, then:

conflicts.incomplete: “{rule}” needs a stage and a stay time of at least 1 hour.
conflicts.beforeLimit: “{rule}” unassigns deals after {hours}h, before the stage “{stage}” stay limit of {limit}h — the overdue alert will never appear for that stage.
conflicts.unreachable: “{blocked}” can never run: “{by}” ({hours}h) already acts first on the same deals. Make one rule more specific with an earlier time, or deactivate one.

automation.howItWorks: Rules are checked automatically every 10 minutes. The clock starts when the deal entered the stage, or when someone last assigned it — whichever is later — so reassigning a deal gives it a fresh window. Deals that are already unassigned are skipped. Unassigning a deal also unassigns its lead, the same as any reassignment. Closed stages (Won, Competitor, Archive) can't have rules. A note counts only if it was written by the currently assigned user after that clock started; the comment written when moving a deal between stages doesn't count. Stay time counts working hours only: Fridays and Saturdays (Cairo time) are not counted, so a deal that entered a stage on Thursday morning has stayed about 24 hours by Sunday morning, not 72.

integrations.title: Integrations & API
integrations.keysDescription: Keys let other software create leads in Acropol. Each key is shown only once, when it is created.
integrations.keyNameHint: What will use this key, e.g. "Website form".
integrations.assignToHint: Optional. Leads created with this key go to this person; otherwise they arrive unassigned.
integrations.keyOnce: Copy this key now — for security it is stored hashed and cannot be shown again.
integrations.deleteConfirm: Delete "{name}"? Anything still using this key will stop working immediately.
integrations.apiDescription: Send a request for each new lead. Authenticate with an API key.
integrations.apiAuth: Send the key as "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY" (or an "X-API-Key" header).
integrations.apiResponses: Responses: 201 = lead created; 200 with status "duplicate" = that phone number already belongs to a lead or customer (nothing is created, the existing record is returned); 400 = invalid data; 401 = missing or invalid key.
integrations.whatsappDescription: Every WhatsApp message sent to your business number creates a lead for the sender.
integrations.waStep1: In Meta for Developers → your app → WhatsApp → Configuration, set the Callback URL above and a Verify token of your choice.
integrations.waStep3: Put the same verify token and the app secret (App settings → Basic) in the server environment, then restart:
integrations.waBehaviour: The sender's WhatsApp name and first message become the lead's name and notes, with source WhatsApp. If the number already belongs to a lead or customer, no new lead is created. Requests are verified with Meta's signature, so only Meta can post here. The URL must be public HTTPS.

gate.title: Turn on notifications to continue
gate.description: Acropol alerts you the moment a deal or lead is assigned to you, when an activity is scheduled, and when one is overdue and still open. These alerts only reach you if browser notifications are on.
gate.promptHint: Your browser will ask for permission — choose Allow. Alerts come with a sound, so keep your volume on.
gate.blockedTitle: Notifications are blocked in this browser
gate.blockedSteps: Click the lock or settings icon next to the address bar, set Notifications to Allow for this site, then come back and press the button below.
